statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays low because CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress rises within the high band after the weekend's Hormuz diplomacy was publicly rejected and Iranian officials restated that the strait stays shut, against a 5.18% 10-year Treasury yield.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the Sunday 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart into the early Asian hours, where the weekend's unpriced diplomatic and military content would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail stays low with futures shut, while the rejection of Iran's seven-day Hormuz plan and Sunday's hardened Tehran statements lift Stress ahead of the 22:00Z restart
body:
Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so no live NQ price path exists at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects absent path risk rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly. The Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42% from a 30,478.86 prior close, mid-range inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range and about half a percent below its 30,770.63 52-week high. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 after a 15.94 session high, and contemporaneous reporting has the Dow up about 0.9% with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite each about 0.5% higher, all three booking weekly gains. That combination shows no shallow-pullback extension, no holding of session extremes and no volatility stress, so the amplifiers this contract requires before Tail reaches the elevated band are absent.

The material change against the previous hour is on the diplomatic leg, and it is the reason Stress moves up rather than Tail. Friday's tape was supported by a concrete de-escalation proposal: Iran's foreign minister offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and restart nuclear talks if the United States lifted its naval blockade, waived sanctions on Iranian oil sales and observed a ceasefire extending to Lebanon. That proposal was rejected on Saturday, with the US president stating that the deal was not acceptable and asserting total control of the strait. Sunday then hardened the position further. A senior Iranian general said the war is not over and that the strait stays closed until US economic pressure ends, the parliament speaker restated the same condition, and the president said Tehran no longer trusts talks with Washington.

Alongside that, the IRGC Navy announced the capture of a second US military REMUS 600 autonomous underwater vehicle in the strait, describing a coordinated intelligence and electronic-warfare operation and transfer to its specialists for data recovery. An army spokesman said the United States may launch a military attack and that Iranian forces are prepared. Saudi authorities moved Riyadh schools to remote learning for a week, and Houthi media reported a Saudi airstrike on Taiz in Yemen. No US or Pentagon response to the drone claim has been published as of this assessment; the September 8 precedent, where the Pentagon characterised a captured Anduril Dive-LD as a malfunctioning older unit holding no sensitive data, is the reference case for a de-escalatory reply.

These items are scored as Stress and uncertainty rather than Tail, for two reasons the contract makes explicit. First, no kinetic strike against shipping or territory has been reported today; the developments are announcements, rhetoric and precaution. Second, the energy market is not confirming an acute supply disruption. WTI settled at $92.41, down 2.33% on Friday and roughly 7.4% across the week, and Brent is quoted near $104 on the shared commodity feed, although contemporaneous Friday reporting on the Brent level is not fully consistent. Falling crude into an active blockade is not escalation pricing. There is also an unresolved factual conflict in the public record, with Tehran restating that the strait is closed while Washington describes large volumes transiting it. That conflict caps Confidence rather than raising Tail.

Rates remain the other standing Stress input. The latest H.15 observation puts the 2-year at 4.87%, the 5-year at 5.03%, the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, with the 10-year at its highest level since the global financial crisis. Equities absorbed that move on Friday without a volatility bid, even as consumer sentiment slipped to a four-month low, which is precisely why the curve is scored as a difficult environment and not as path risk.

Shared latest-session context is stale beyond its 90-minute freshness bound and only partially collected, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it is treated as delayed colour only and cannot establish current NQ structure. What it does show is mixed rather than uniformly aligned: megacaps six of eight higher with roughly 1.9% dispersion and semiconductors six of seven higher, alongside a 0.85% technology sector gain against a 0.58% decline in communication services. Mixed breadth of that kind lowers directional conviction; it does not mechanically raise Tail.

The one genuine forward amplifier is mechanical rather than observed, and it is now better defined than an hour ago. Friday's close embedded reopening optimism that the weekend has removed, so the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart is where an identified negative delta meets thin Sunday-evening liquidity. A narrow danger window is published from there into 02:00Z, with conditional Tail peaking at 17 in the first full hour after the restart and the mode set to event/whipsaw for two-way repricing rather than an assumed direction. Beyond it the week is dense but well defined: JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence on Tuesday, ADP with Core PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, Micron's fiscal Q4 report after Wednesday's cash close, ISM Manufacturing and jobless claims on Thursday and September payrolls on Friday at 12:30Z. Every one of those items is a checkpoint, not an automatic block, and none is scored here as observed structure.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were left unchanged. Tail held in a narrow 6-8 range, Stress rose from 48 to 65 and Confidence decayed from 81 to 71 across the period, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a weekend with no live price discovery and an increasingly demanding rates, oil and geopolitical backdrop. The mapped state remained EA_ON throughout, and the dominant mode stayed normal because no slot in the window contained observable one-way structure.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours. Risk holds near the closed-period baseline through the remainder of Sunday, then lifts from roughly 18:00Z into a published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart, where the weekend's rejected Hormuz proposal and hardened Tehran statements meet thin liquidity, peaking at 17 in the first full hour after the restart with the mode set to event/whipsaw for two-way repricing. It then decays through the Asian hours on the base assumption that restart pricing is absorbed with normal two-way discovery, and Stress eases into the elevated band by the European session. Confidence troughs just before the restart while the evidence set ages without refreshing observation, then recovers once a live NQ price path exists again. Every value after the current clock-hour is conditional: no post-restart gap, continuation, failed retracement or extension has been observed, and any such structure would supersede this published path.
